method: AI-assisted visual comparison of each complete judgment, including continuation pages. OCR used only to locate passages. This is one review pass, not independent human scholarly certification.

ingestion.note: New scan agreement does not establish the historical digital ingestion source.

witness.title: The Sacred Books of China: The Texts of Confucianism. Part II: The Yî King
witness.series: The Sacred Books of the East, XVI
witness.catalogueScope: Four-volume set, not the imprint date of this volume

rightsMetadata.note: IA metadata's 2008 no-visible-notice statement is attributed metadata. Both visually inspected title pages actually print [All rights reserved]. No broader legal opinion or claim about modern transcriptions is made.

retainedDifferences: Existing ASCII romanizations are retained; original diacritics and italic consonant distinctions are not restored.
Historical 3-shaped consonant glyphs remain represented as Z; no claim of glyph identity.
Original letterspacing, paragraphs, end-of-line hyphens, apostrophe styles and spacing around punctuation are normalized.
In hexagram 51 the original measure lî remains li.
transcription.note: This states visible differences in the existing website text, not an inferred original editorial policy.
transcription.notationLegend: K* and Z* in the records denote letters printed in italic type in the original; the asterisk is review notation, not an original character. The phrase 3-shaped initial describes a historical glyph without assigning an unverified Unicode identity.

hashRule: SHA-256 of UTF-8 JSON.stringify of the 64 displayed judgments in King Wen order; source labels excluded.
